artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space, and denote by $\mathcal{K}(X,X)$ the Banach space of compact linear operators from $X$ to $X$, equipped with the operator norm, and by $B_{\mathcal{K}(X,X)}$ its closed unit ball. Recall the following.

(i) $X$ is said to have the metric compact approximation property (MCAP) if for every compact set $K \subset X$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $T \in B_{\mathcal{K}(X,X)}$ (i.e., a compact operator with $\|T\| \leq 1$) such that $\|Tx - x\| \leq \varepsilon$ for all $x \in K$.

(ii) Let $X^* \hat{\otimes}_\pi X$ denote the projective tensor product of $X^*$ and $X$. The trace mapping
$$V : X^* \hat{\otimes}_\pi X \longrightarrow \mathcal{K}(X,X)^*$$
is the bounded linear map defined on elementary tensors by $V(x^* \otimes x)(T) = x^*(Tx)$ for $x^* \in X^*$, $x \in X$, $T \in \mathcal{K}(X,X)$, and extended by linearity and continuity.

Question: Is it true that $X$ has the metric compact approximation property if and only if the trace mapping $V : X^* \hat{\otimes}_\pi X \to \mathcal{K}(X,X)^*$ is an isometry (i.e., $\|V(u)\| = \|u\|_\pi$ for all $u \in X^* \hat{\otimes}_\pi X$)?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution of this characterization of the metric compact approximation property in terms of the isometry of the trace mapping $X^*\hat{\otimes}_\pi X \to \mathcal{K}(X,X)^*$. Related work on compact approximation properties and tensor product trace dualities exists, but no source clearly settles this specific equivalence in the affirmative or negative, so the status is taken to be unverified.

status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of approximation properties via projective tensor products and trace duality with K(X,X), without giving the stated MCAP equivalence.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference treats trace duality but does not resolve this specific MCAP characterization.

status_evidence.title: Approximation property in terms of Lipschitz maps via tensor product approach
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper studying approximation properties through tensor product trace mappings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to investigate trace-mapping characterizations of approximation properties, suggesting the MCAP version is not a settled folklore result.
